opening_message:
Ticket 1: Mary Lee (employee ID E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E015.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. Full-time employees max out at write, and admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system (Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Analyst). Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. IT DB confirms role: Analyst. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max out at write. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max out at write. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms E015 role: Analyst. Mary Lee is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max out at write. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms E015 role: Analyst. Mary Lee is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Analyst, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max out at write. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent, note 5 by Facilities agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Mary Lee (E015) is a contractor with basic security training (not full-time as other notes suggest). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum of read, so recommend granting read.
reason: Mary Lee (E015) requested admin access to Source Code. The Security agent, who looked up the employment type in their own database, reports that Mary Lee is a contractor with basic security training — not full-time as the other notes assumed (those agents did not verify employment type). Per policy, contractors may have read access, or write only with advanced security training, and never admin. With only basic security training, the maximum allowed level is read. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Mary Lee (E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

Most notes say she's a full-time Analyst, but the Security agent says she's a contractor with basic security training. The Security agent looked up employment type and security training in their own database. The other agents did not look up employment type (they said "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1").

The Security agent is the one who looked up employment type specifically, and has unique data on security training. Security DB shows contractor with basic security training.

So the relevant facts: contractor, basic security training.

Policy for contractors: read, or write only if advanced security training. Never admin.

Requested: admin. Maximum: read (since basic training, not advanced). So grant read.

Wait - contractor with basic security training: read or write if advanced training. So maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds max, grant max = read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit.
